findings.evidence: TauCeti/Analysis/Fredholm/LevelSet/Basic.lean:271-274: `levelSetChartModel ... (ha : f a = c) : OpenPartialHomeomorph ↥{x | f x = c} (Fin n → 𝕜)`.
findings.fix: Say "a neighbourhood of `ξ₀` in the level set of the section through `ξ₀`", or add "when the section vanishes at `ξ₀`".
findings.issue: The module docstring says that when the trajectory operator is Fredholm and surjective, "a neighbourhood of `ξ₀` in the zero set of the section" is charted by `TauCeti.levelSetChartModel`. That chart covers the level set through `ξ₀`, which is the zero set only when the section vanishes at `ξ₀`.

findings.evidence: The diff defines `hasStrictFDerivAt_trajectorySection_of_isBounded_range_of_continuous [ProperSpace F] ... (hV'c : Continuous V')`. The Main declarations list stops at `..._of_isBounded_range`.
findings.fix: Cite `hasStrictFDerivAt_trajectorySection_of_isBounded_range_of_continuous` for the continuous case, say "proper" rather than only finite-dimensional, and add it to the Main declarations list.
findings.issue: The module docstring credits the "continuous on a finite-dimensional space" case to `hasStrictFDerivAt_trajectorySection_of_isBounded_range`, which assumes `∀ r, UniformContinuousOn V' (ball 0 r)`. The continuous case is the separate `hasStrictFDerivAt_trajectorySection_of_isBounded_range_of_continuous` (on a `ProperSpace`), which is also missing from "Main declarations".

summary: Docstrings are present and mostly accurate, but the Section module docstring misdescribes the chart as covering the zero set at an arbitrary ξ₀ and credits the finite-dimensional case to the wrong theorem.
